parsed.explanation: A trans visitor faces documented state targeting: broad immigration removal for perceived queerness without conviction, morality/sex-work prosecutions carrying prison, dating-app entrapment especially of trans women, custody abuse and coerced examinations, with authorities indifferent and media incitement. No anti-discrimination protection, healthcare discrimination is pervasive, and legal gender recognition is being closed nationwide. Deportation or detention/abuse after outing is credibly documented, execution is not. This is organised, current state exposure, not merely social disapproval.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior ministry may refuse entry/removal for disturbing public order/morality; documented deportations of foreign nationals suspected gay/trans without upheld charges, 12 incidents 2018-2022 analysed 2023.
entry_documents.interaction: Perceived queerness or document/presentation mismatch can trigger morality referral; effect of 2024 marker-recognition closure on foreign passports is unresolved.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Dating-app entrapment by police, blackmail and arrests, especially trans women; violations and physical abuse in stations, coerced anal examinations, dark cells/beatings historically, at least 84 arrests in 2017.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: App encounter or complaint can become morality prosecution, prolonged detention, abuse, then deportation or prison sentence.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No specific bathroom, ward or custody-placement rule is sourced; vague public-morality enforcement could affect any public gendered space, but that application is not documented.

care_services.exposure: Healthcare access restricted on identity grounds; 2025 review submission reports pervasive gender-identity discrimination and persistent barriers to equitable services for trans residents.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care after outing risks disclosure, refusal or delay, compounding detention and travel disruption; no visitor care guarantee is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Morality, debauchery and 1961 sex-work provisions read to criminalise habitual same-sex conduct with prison sentences; official/media incitement accompanied arrests; relationship read as same-sex may be used under Satanism/prostitution/immorality laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing treats gender/sexual nonconformity as public-morality threat, licensing police, immigration and media action combined.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific travel, custody or care rule for trans minors or guardians is sourced; adult visitor exposure above applies to accompanying adults.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police are documented perpetrators via entrapment, blackmail and custody abuse, with authorities turning a blind eye; undated survey cited 95% non-acceptance of homosexuality as background hostility.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police risks being targeted; public hostility and incitement increase chance an outing escalates rather than receiving protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statutory anti-discrimination protection on SOGIESC grounds; removal requires no conviction; no effective remedy documented for deported visitors.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse makes immigration, policing and healthcare exposures unremedied; unresolved points include foreign-marker treatment and currency of undated entrapment reporting.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: sweeps/entrapment, prolonged detention, officer violence, public-order charges and ineffective recourse. This dossier lacks a documented capital clause and visitor imprisonment is less uniformly shown than deportation, so slightly above 0.15.

More severe than 0.25-A: there prison is rare and execution absent, with occasional overturned convictions. Here morality arrests explicitly carry prison, deportation without charge is documented, and custody abuse/forced examinations recur, placing it materially below 0.25.

Far below 0.35-B, where detention is hours-long, fines are typical and imprisonment uncommon. Here organised entrapment, physical abuse in custody, coerced examinations and prison sentences make the post-outing pathway much more dangerous.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is nationally uniform: immigration morality discretion, criminalisation through sex-work/morality provisions, and police entrapment interact across the journey. A visitor need not be convicted to be deported; if detained, documented abuse and forced examination are possible, and prosecution can carry prison. No operative protection, anti-discrimination remedy or healthcare guarantee offsets this. Execution is not documented and the most recent dated forced-examination arrest is 2017, preventing a 0.05 rating, but 2023-2026 sources show the legal and policing pattern continuing.
